title: What Are You Doing After Graduation?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I've been thinking a lot about what I'm going to do after graduation. I've been training for three years. I want to use it.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Are you going to apply for the sports science programme in Almaty? You've been talking about it since last year.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I was. But I've changed my mind. I had been assuming I wanted to coach. But I've realised I want to work in sports analytics.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: That's a big change. What changed?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I've been doing data analysis for the volleyball team since February — tracking performance, injury patterns. I love it. More than I love coaching.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: I had no idea you'd been doing that. How long have you been doing it?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Since the start of the spring semester. The coach asked me to try it. I haven't stopped since.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: So you've completely changed your direction while we've all been assuming you knew exactly where you were going.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Yes. While I've been practising every morning, I've also been discovering what I actually want to do. They happened at the same time.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: What about you, Rustam? You've been very quiet.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: I've been avoiding this conversation. I don't know what I want. I've been studying economics for three years and I'm still not sure why.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: My father has been running his own business since before I was born. He's always assumed I'll take it over. I've never told him I don't want to.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Have you been thinking about what you do want?

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: I've been writing. Essays, mainly. Not for university — just for myself. I don't know if that counts as a plan.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: It counts as something. Something you've been doing without being told to. That's usually the thing that matters.

questions.text: "I had been assuming I wanted to coach." — "had been assuming" means:
opts: She just changed her mind now
Before changing her mind, this had been her ongoing assumption for some time
She will assume it in the future
questions.correct: Before changing her mind, this had been her ongoing assumption for some time
questions.hint: "had been assuming" = Past Perfect Continuous. Ongoing assumption BEFORE the change of mind. ✅

questions.text: "I haven't stopped since." — This uses Present Perfect because:
opts: The action is in the past
The action started in the past and continues to now
She will stop in the future
questions.correct: The action started in the past and continues to now
questions.hint: "haven't stopped" = Present Perfect negative. Started the analytics work and has NOT stopped — the continuation is the point. ✅

questions.text: "He's always assumed I'll take it over." — "has always assumed" expresses:
opts: An ongoing state or attitude throughout a period up to now
A past habit that has stopped
questions.correct: An ongoing state or attitude throughout a period up to now
questions.hint: "has always assumed" = Present Perfect with "always" showing a persistent attitude throughout the past up to now. ✅

questions.text: "I ___ (write) for myself since my first year." Use the correct tense.
questions.hint: Duration started in the past, still ongoing → Present Perfect Continuous. "I HAVE BEEN WRITING for myself since my first year." ✅
